text:
jordan: Quick heads-up — we pushed a kernel-hint tweak yesterday and perf-ci flagged a ~3% p95 regression on MQA-heavy inference (hosted). Not catastrophic but reproducible on canary clusters.

perf-ci: [alert] p95_latency: +3.1% (baseline 88ms -> 90.7ms) on mqa-seqworkload-prod, suspects: kernel-picker change #448.

marta: Ugh. Any flamegraphs / top stacks?

jordan: Pasted a trimmed flame: https://perf.internal/redwood/fg/3198765432 — main hotspot is paged_attn_block::read_block + hot path in kvcache_pagewalker. Also L2 miss counter spiked in the canary run.

ryan: Can you paste the microbench command you used to reproduce? I'll run locally.

jordan: Sure:```bash
./bench/mqa_microbench --model gqa-mqa-48n --seq 1024 --batch 16 --kvcache-page-size 32 --kernel-hints thermostat
```

jordan: With that, tail shows frequent small pagewalks when seqlen > 512 and gqa>8. Seems the kernel pick prefers the paged-kv-block variant with block_sz=32 which increases pointer chasing.

marta: Hmm. We landed an autotuner change to prefer smaller block sizes for warm caching, that might interact poorly with multi-q layout.

autotuner-bot: Started new sweep job autotune/3198765432: param grid {block_sz: [32,48,64,128], prefetch: [on,off], kernel_policy: [thermostat,latency,throughput]} on runner-a-05. Estimated run time 3h.

ryan: I'll run an ablation matrix across seq bins: [64,256,512,1024,2048] to see where the cross-over occurs. If block_sz=32 loses to 64 for seqlen>=768 then autotuner needs seqlen-conditioned scoring.

jordan: Agreed. Preliminary local numbers: block32/prefetch-on p95=92ms, block64/prefetch-on p95=89ms for seq1024 batch16. L2 misses: block32 +14%, block64 +6%.

marta: Do we have a quick patch: prefer block64 when avg_seq >= 700 or when gqa>12? That would be a short-term guard.

ryan: I can throw a gating heuristic in kernel-scorer: add a term score += -10 if block_sz < 64 and avg_seq > 700. Won't be perfect but cheap. I'll push a canary.

jordan: Also let's add telemetry: emit chosen_kernel + block_sz + avg_seq histogram per route so we can validate in prod.

autotuner-bot: Sweep job autotune/3198765432 completed: best config block_sz=64 prefetch=on kernel_policy=thermostat for seq buckets >= 768. Improvement vs current: -2.6% p95 on canary.

marta: Nice. Can we adjust the autotuner scoring so it returns a conditional policy (block_sz by seq bucket) instead of single global pick?

jordan: Yes — we already have the scoring model with feature vector {avg_seq, gqa, batch, hw_arch}. Update is to output per-bucket picks. Requires small change in config schema.

ryan: I pushed canary kernel-scorer with the naive gate (PR #482). Canaries on canary1 show p95 back to baseline. Running full sweep overnight.

perf-ci: [update] canary1 p95: 88.9ms (within noise).

jordan: If overnight sweep looks stable, let's ship kernel-scorer gate + telemetry, and schedule a proper autotune run to produce bucketized picks. Also add a regression test: microbench runs for seqlen {256,1024,2048} should not regress >1% p95 after change.

marta: I'll own the autotune job to produce the bucketized mapping and update release notes.

ryan: I'll follow up with a short doc in docs/ops about the 'thermostat' kernel policy and its interaction with paged-KV.

jordan: Thanks team. Action items: ryan (gate PR + nightly ablation), marta (bucketized autotune + release notes), jordan (telemetry + regression test).

marta: :thumbsup:

ryan: FYI if anyone wants to reproduce: I used perf counters via `nvprof --metrics l2_cache_transactions` and `perf record` for CPU side. Happy to share commands.

jordan: Share them here and I'll bake into the repro script.

ryan:```bash
# nvprof on gpu node
nvprof --metrics l2_cache_transactions ./bench/mqa_microbench ...
# perf on host
perf record -e L1-dcache-load-misses,L1-dcache-loads -o perf.data -- ./bench/mqa_microbench ...
```

marta: Good progress. Keep thread updated if the overnight sweep finds any other cross-overs (esp. gqa>24).
